text:
aya: FYI - after last night's firewall baseline roll (eu-west), we're seeing a wave of GPU node evictions in the warm pool starting ~08:13 UTC. 15% capacity loss so far. KMS decrypt p99 jumped to ~2.1s and audit-shipper queue length spiked.

mike: ugh. any correlation with natgw CPU/conntrack?

aya: yes - natgw connections peaked around the same time. flow logs show repeated retries to 10.18.4.22 (keystore proxy).

jamie: can someone paste the exact fw rule change? I need to confirm if we started dropping egress to our keystore CIDR.

aya: the rule was: allowlist only -> deny-by-default for all egress except approved endpoints. looks like keystore proxy IPs weren't on the allowlist for eu-west canary.

priya: deploy-bot reports: "terraform apply complete: module/fw-baseline (eu-west)". :grimacing:

deploy-bot: terraform apply successful (plan id: plan-8823).

mike: immediate mitigation options? rollback? temporary allowlist?

aya: short-term: add keystore proxy range to fw allowlist and scale natgw/min-workers. long-term: we need an egress test in CI that hits keystore horizontally.

jamie: +1. I'm patching the rule now to allow 10.18.4.0/24 for keystore and HSM endpoints. will push a canary in 2m.

sre-bot: Alert: eu-warmpool-gpu-node-count decreased by 123 over 5m. KMS p50=120ms p95=900ms p99=2.1s.

priya: re: audit-shipper backlog - it's saturated the natgw bandwidth. if we allowlist, backlog will drain but might still need exporter throttling. any objections to reducing retention to 1d for staging shipper temporarily?

mike: do it. reduce retention and throttle to 20% of production QPS.

aya: canary result: keystore latency back to baseline after allowlist, warm-pool rejoining started. patch id: fw-allow-10-18-4 applied.

jamie: rolling the firewall change to the rest of eu regions but adding pre-check to ensure keystore IPs are present. also adding a gating `curl` healthcheck to deploy pipeline:

```
# pre-deploy check
curl -sS https://keystore-eu-west.health.redwood-internal/status | jq .decrypt_latency_ms
if [ "$DECRYPT_LATENCY_MS" -gt 500 ]; then
  echo "block deploy - keystore latency high"; exit 1;
fi
```

mike: good. also let's add a canary to the warm pool: when KMS p99 > 1s, auto-scale warm-pool down to prevent noisy neighbor evictions. Put on-call runbook update.

priya: opened runbook PR for audit-shipper throttling + temporary retention. linking in the incident ticket.

deploy-bot: Rollout note: reverted fw baseline in eu-west canary -> allowlist patch applied.

aya: post-mortem action items: 1) add egress allowlist check to infra CI 2) add keystore IPs to global fw template 3) add KMS latency alert that ties to warm-pool policy 4) audit-shipper backpressure mitigation (throttle + retention fallback).

jamie: agree. estimating 3 dev-days across infra + security to implement.

mike: cost note: temporary natgw scale + audit export draining will bump monthly S3/egress by an estimated $4k for the month if not reverted. flagging finance.

priya: FYI to security - marking this as compliance-impacting since audit logs were delayed. @security-team please confirm if we need to extend retention windows for legal hold.

aya: thanks everyone. keep monitoring, i'll post a health check in 15m. :thumbsup:
